analysis.one_liner: Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone (APSEZ) runs India's largest private port network and is building out adjacent logistics, marine/shipping, and international port businesses (Israel, Sri Lanka, Tanzania, Oman).
analysis.whats_happening: Q2 FY27 results (quarter ended Sep 2026), announced 28 Oct 2026: revenue up 24% YoY to Rs 11,340 cr, EBITDA up 23% to Rs 6,807 cr, PAT up 18% to Rs 3,682 cr. Management raised FY27 revenue guidance by Rs 1,000 cr to Rs 44,000-46,000 cr, EBITDA guidance by Rs 1,000 cr, and capex guidance by Rs 3,000 cr to Rs 15,000-17,000 cr. The stock rose on the print and sits near its 52-week high. Earlier in October the company also incorporated an Oman subsidiary (Indian Ocean Gateway Terminal) as part of its international port push.
analysis.plain_terms: Adani Ports operates India's biggest private port network and is layering on logistics, shipping, and overseas ports around that core. Revenue and operating profit (EBITDA) grew a strong 23-24% in the latest quarter, but net profit grew more slowly at 18% - some of the operating gain is being absorbed by costs below the operating line, likely tied to the heavy capex underway. The stock trades near its all-time high at roughly 31 times earnings, which prices in continued strong growth rather than an obviously cheap entry point.
analysis.quarters: Q2 FY27 (Sep 2026): revenue Rs 11,340 cr (+24% YoY), EBITDA Rs 6,807 cr (+23% YoY, ~60% margin), PAT Rs 3,682 cr (+18% YoY). H1 FY27: revenue Rs 22,161 cr (+21%), EBITDA Rs 13,347 cr (+21%), PAT Rs 7,332 cr (+14%) - PAT growth has trailed EBITDA growth for two straight quarters, consistent with rising finance costs/depreciation as the balance sheet gears up for expansion, not a restatement or accounting shift. Domestic ports remain the profit engine: Rs 7,177 cr revenue (+13%) at a 72.5% EBITDA margin. International ports grew revenue 71% and EBITDA 236% YoY, but off a much smaller base (47.7% EBITDA margin, described as a 'record') - a high growth rate that isn't yet representative of the larger domestic business. Management raised FY27 revenue and EBITDA guidance by Rs 1,000 cr each and capex guidance by Rs 3,000 cr.
analysis.performance_read: The stock is near its all-time high (Rs 1,850 vs a peak of Rs 1,883.2, just 1.8% off), so there is no crash or meaningful drawdown to explain here. Returns have compounded strongly and well ahead of the market: 27.4% over 1 year (Nifty: -10.9%), 138.9% over 3 years (Nifty: 20.8%), and 169.8% over 5 years (Nifty: 28.6%), also beating peer JSWINFRA (102.4% over 5 years). The only corporate action on record is a 2010 5:1 stock split, which does not distort these multi-year return figures - there is no demerger or spin-off adjustment needed.
analysis.valuation_read: At Rs 1,850 the stock trades around 30.8x trailing earnings and roughly 4.2x book value - a clear premium versus typical infrastructure names. That premium exists because the business combines a very high-margin domestic ports core (72.5% EBITDA margin), genuine international diversification, and a management team that keeps revising guidance upward. Whether the premium is justified is separate from why it exists: a 31x multiple is pricing in several more years of double-digit EBITDA growth, so any slowdown in cargo volumes or a stall in the newer international/logistics/marine segments would compress it quickly.
analysis.growth_read: Growth is a mix of volume-led and margin-led, but unevenly spread across the business. The core domestic ports segment grew a more modest 13% in revenue with a stable, already-high EBITDA margin - durable, cargo-volume-driven growth. International ports and marine grew much faster (71% and 57% revenue growth respectively) but off smaller bases, with margins still being built out. This means the group's headline 24% revenue growth is partly flattered by smaller, faster-growing newer segments rather than being fully replicable at the core.
analysis.health_read: Operating cash generation looks solid on the numbers available - EBITDA margin near 60% and H1 free cash flow of Rs 2,806 cr - suggesting profits are largely converting to cash, though a full cash-flow-statement reconciliation is Not verified - check on Screener. The debt profile is moderate: debt-to-equity of 0.56x and net debt/EBITDA of 1.8x, both manageable, but FY27 capex guidance was just raised by Rs 3,000 cr to fund continued port, logistics, marine fleet, and international expansion. The risk here reads more as execution/business risk (can the newer, lower-margin segments scale) than acute balance-sheet risk, but leverage metrics are worth rechecking each quarter as that capex lands.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoters hold 66.03% of the company as of September 2026, and the promoter group has formally confirmed no shares are pledged for FY26. On governance: SEBI closed its Hindenburg-related adjudication proceedings in September 2026 via a settlement (Rs 1.51 crore total across five Adani group entities, without admission of wrongdoing), having earlier found the core market-manipulation allegations unsubstantiated. Separately, the unrelated US bribery case against Gautam Adani personally was dismissed by a US judge in 2026, though related charges remain pending against some Adani Group executives - that matter concerns Adani Green Energy's solar contracts, not Adani Ports' business directly, but it remains a group-level reputational overhang worth knowing about. No standout marquee independent investor was flagged in available sources on this register - Not verified - check on Screener for the full institutional holder list.
strengths: Domestic ports EBITDA margin of 72.5%, among the highest in the sector, alongside steady 13% revenue growth in that segment
FY27 revenue and EBITDA guidance raised by Rs 1,000 cr each after a strong H1 (EBITDA +21% YoY to Rs 13,347 cr)
Net debt/EBITDA of 1.8x and debt-to-equity of 0.56x - manageable leverage despite a heavy capex cycle
Promoter holding of 66.03% with zero pledge confirmed for FY26
watchpoints: PAT growth (18% YoY in Q2) has trailed EBITDA growth (23%) for two straight quarters, likely rising finance costs/depreciation from expansion capex
Valuation at ~31x P/E and ~4.2x P/B prices in sustained double-digit growth - a volume slowdown would compress the multiple quickly
FY27 capex guidance just raised by Rs 3,000 cr to Rs 15,000-17,000 cr - leverage trend needs monitoring as this spend lands
International ports' 236% EBITDA growth is off a small base and margin (47.7%) is still well below the domestic business (72.5%) - not yet representative of the group
analysis.one_thing: Whether PAT growth re-converges with EBITDA growth in H2 FY27 will show whether the current capex-driven expansion is being funded without structurally diluting bottom-line margins.
